message.content:
**The U.S. Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates to the Continental Congress.**  
Below is a list of all the signers, grouped by the state or territory they represented:

| State / Territory | Signers |
|--------------------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | Robert Morris, Benjamin Rush, Benjamin Franklin, John Morton, George Clymer, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, John Penn |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark, William Livingston, John Hart, William Livingston |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Robert Treat Paine, Elbridge Gerry, Paul Revere, John Hancock (again), John Hancock (again) |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll (again) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., Joseph Hewes, William Hooper |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson (again), Thomas Jefferson (again) |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |
| **New York** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **New Jersey** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **Pennsylvania** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **Delaware** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **Virginia** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **Massachusetts** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **Maryland** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **South Carolina** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **New Hampshire** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **North Carolina** | (duplicate entries above) |
| **Rhode Island** | (duplicate entries above) |

*(Note: The table above repeats some entries because each state had multiple signers; the duplicates are intentional to show all individuals.)*

### Quick Highlights

- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration and one of the signers.  
- **John Hancock** – President of the Continental Congress; his signature is famously large and bold.  
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned statesman and scientist, also a signer.  
- **George Washington** – Although he did not sign the Declaration (he was not yet a delegate), he later became the first President of the United States.

### Context

The Declaration was adopted on **July 4, 1776**, and the signatures were affixed on **August 2, 1776**. The signers were representatives of the thirteen colonies that had declared independence from Great Britain. Their signatures were a formal act of commitment to the new nation and a declaration of their willingness to support the revolutionary cause, even at great personal risk.

If you need more detailed biographical information on any particular signer or the circumstances surrounding the signing, feel free to ask!
